elements.quote: Global Prevalence of COVID-19-Associated Mucormycosis (CAM): Living Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis ... Keywords: coinfection; COVID-19; epidemiology; meta-analysis; mucormycosis; mycoses; prevalence; risk factors; systematic review
elements.reason: The title and keywords explicitly identify the report as a systematic review (and meta-analysis).

elements.quote: This study aims to compute the pooled prevalence of CAM and other associated clinical outcomes.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main objective explicitly.

elements.quote: All studies reporting the prevalence of mucormycosis among COVID-19 patients were eligible for inclusion.
elements.reason: The main inclusion (eligibility) criterion is specified in the abstract.

elements.quote: MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane COVID-19 Study Register, and WHO COVID-19 databases were scanned to retrieve the relevant articles until August 2021.
elements.reason: Information sources and the date of the last search (August 2021) are reported.

elements.quote: Two investigators independently screened the articles against the selection criteria, extracted the data, and performed the quality assessment using the JBI tool.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies risk of bias assessment using the JBI tool.

elements.quote: Comprehensive Meta-Analysis software version 2 was used for performing the meta-analysis.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the synthesis method (meta-analysis using CMA software).

elements.quote: This meta-analysis comprised six studies with a pooled sample size of 52,916 COVID-19 patients with a mean age of 62.12 ± 9.69 years.
elements.reason: Total number of studies and participants plus study characteristics (mean age, onset duration) are reported.

elements.quote: The pooled prevalence of CAM (seven cases per 1000 patients) was 50 times higher than the highest recorded background of mucormycosis (0.14 cases per 1000 patients). A high mortality rate was found among CAM patients with a pooled prevalence rate of 29.6% (95% CI: 17.2-45.9%).
elements.reason: Results for the primary and secondary outcomes (CAM prevalence, mortality) are presented.

elements.quote: A high mortality rate was found among CAM patients with a pooled prevalence rate of 29.6% (95% CI: 17.2-45.9%).
elements.reason: A meta-analysis was conducted and the abstract reports a pooled estimate with its 95% confidence interval (mortality); the pooled CAM prevalence is also given.
No groups are compared in this review of prevalence; no comparative effect direction applies.
The abstract does not mention any limitations of the included evidence such as risk of bias, inconsistency (e.g., high I²), or imprecision.

elements.quote: Optimal glycemic control and the judicious use of steroids should be the approach for tackling rising CAM cases.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation and implications of the findings.
The abstract does not state the funding source for the review.
The abstract provides no registration name or registration number.
No retrieved evidence from the introduction/rationale describes the current state of knowledge or uncertainties about CAM prevalence.
No retrieved evidence explains the importance of or need for conducting this review.
No retrieved evidence cites or discusses prior systematic reviews to justify this update; the living review section (text_11) does not identify previous reviews.
This is a review of prevalence (etiology), not of intervention effects, so no mechanism of action is required.
This is a prevalence meta-analysis, not a review of complex interventions, so a logic model is not applicable.

elements.quote: The primary outcome of this meta-analysis was to compute the pooled global prevalence of CAM. The secondary outcome was to compute the pooled prevalence of diabetes, steroid use, and mortality among CAM patients.
elements.reason: The review's objectives are explicitly stated (pooled global prevalence of CAM and secondary prevalences), but they are not framed using a question-formulation framework (e.g., PICO or similar); only outcome-based objectives are reported.

elements.quote: The primary outcome of this meta-analysis was to compute the pooled global prevalence of CAM.
elements.reason: This is a review of prevalence (etiology/frequency), not of intervention effects, so planned PICO-style intervention comparisons do not apply.

elements.quote: We included cross-sectional or longitudinal studies reporting the prevalence of mucormycosis among confirmed COVID-19 patients (based on RT-PCR reports). Only studies with confirmed mucormycosis cases diagnosed based on the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention criteria... were qualified for inclusion. Case reports, case series, reviews or studies with incomplete information about the confirmed number of mucormycosis cases from the total number of COVID-19 patients were excluded.

No report characteristics such as publication year range, language restrictions, or publication status are reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The subgroup analysis was performed based on diabetes as a comorbidity, and steroid exposure.

Restrictions (e.g., excluding case reports/series, requiring CDC diagnostic criteria) are stated but no rationale for these restrictions is provided.

elements.quote: Two reviewers (S.H. and A.R.) independently scanned all the retrieved articles initially based on title and abstract, followed by full-text readings in the later phase. All the articles were judged against the inclusion and exclusion parameters described in the eligibility criteria.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the general study selection process (dual independent screening, judging against eligibility criteria, third-reviewer arbitration) and the flow into the meta-analysis (text_13: 'only six studies met the inclusion criteria for inclusion in the meta-analysis'; PRISMA flowchart in figure_11 shows exclusion reasons such as 'Outcome not of interest' and 'Study design not of interest'). However, there is no description of processes used to decide eligibility specifically for each synthesis, such as tabulating study characteristics and comparing them against planned synthesis groups. Only a single synthesis (pooled prevalence meta-analysis) is evident, and the per-synthesis decision process is not explicitly described.

The retrieved evidence describes software, effect model, heterogeneity thresholds, sensitivity and subgroup analyses (text_12) and data extraction items (text_8), but nowhere describes methods for preparing data for synthesis, such as handling of missing summary statistics or data conversions (e.g., converting proportions/counts to prevalence estimates).

elements.quote: The strength of this meta-analysis was an exhaustive literature search and inclusion of only confirmed CAM patients, which makes the evidence more robust. All the studies from India had a unique set of patients as the study period and the hospital centres varied.

elements.quote: The findings of this meta-analysis warrant future epidemiologic studies on CAM patients to precisely report the vaccination rates and characteristics among all COVID-19 patients under investigation in order to facilitate the evaluation of the role of vaccines in modifying the risks of morbidity and mortality.
